column3: “To offer, along with the prayers” renders “that he will give [it] with the prayers”; BSB moves “who had a golden censer” forward.
BSB follows the critical-text order “thunder, rumblings, lightning”; “hurled” renders ἔβαλεν (“cast”).
“To sound them” renders “that they may sound the trumpets.”
BSB follows the critical text with “A third of the earth was burned up,” which the Textus Receptus lacks. “Hurled down” renders “was cast.”
BSB adds “bitter like … oil” and “bitter” before “waters”; the Greek says “became wormwood” and “because they were made bitter.”
“A third of the stars were darkened” renders “so that a third of them may be darkened,” which refers to all three.
BSB follows the critical text with “an eagle” (the Textus Receptus has “an angel”). “Trumpet blasts” renders “voices of the trumpet.”
